reading.title: Why Dogs Hide Things
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文不复述课文里的 pub 和狗的故事，而是讲一个真实的科学话题：狗为什么爱把东西叼走、藏起来。内容改编自权威科普媒体 Live Science 的报道，介绍源自狼祖先的 food caching（藏食）本能。
passage: When a dog drags a shoe behind the sofa or buries a treat in a flower bed, it is not simply misbehaving; it is acting on an inheritance written deep into its biology. Scientists call this impulse food caching, and one common form of it is known as scatter-hoarding, in which an animal conceals surplus supplies across many separate hiding places rather than piling everything into a single store. The behaviour is ancient. The domestic dog descends from the grey wolf, a predator whose meals were anything but predictable. After a successful hunt a wolf might find far more meat than it could eat at once, so concealing the leftovers was a sensible insurance policy against the lean days that were certain to follow.

Evidence for these deep roots reaches back decades. A 1976 study published in the journal Ethology recorded wolves burying the remains of their kills, and even observed wolf pups stashing food and later relocating their hoards so that hungry siblings could not pilfer them. Such relocation is striking, since it shows that the pups could return to the exact spot days later and successfully retrieve what they had hidden. Modern pets rarely face genuine hunger, yet the instinct endures. As the trainer Teoti Anderson observes, when you cannot predict your next meal, hiding the leftovers makes perfect sense. Today the same urge may surface as savouring a cherished toy, relieving anxiety, or, in breeds such as terriers and dachshunds bred to dig, an irrepressible compulsion to excavate the nearest patch of soft earth.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to train a dog to stop digging up the garden.
Which dog breeds make the best family pets.
Why dogs hide objects, and how the habit traces back to their wolf ancestors.
The difference between wild wolves and modern pet dogs.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕狗藏东西（food caching / scatter-hoarding）这一行为，并解释它源自灰狼祖先的生存本能，所以主旨是“狗为什么藏东西，以及这一习惯如何追溯到狼祖先”。

questions.question: According to the passage, what is 'scatter-hoarding'?
options: Hiding surplus food in many separate places instead of one single store.
Eating all available food at once before it can be stolen.
Burying food only in a single, carefully chosen location.
Sharing leftover food equally among the pack.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文说 scatter-hoarding 指动物把多余食物分散藏在许多不同地点，而不是堆在一个仓库里。

questions.question: Why did wolves cache leftover meat after a hunt?
options: Because they preferred the taste of buried, aged meat.
Because their den was too small to keep food inside.
Because other predators ordered them to share it.
Because their food supply was unpredictable, so saving meat protected them against lean days.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文说狼的食物来源很不稳定，一次猎到的肉可能吃不完，把剩肉藏起来是为应对随后必然到来的“饥荒日”，是一种保险。

questions.question: What can we infer about wolves that relocate their hidden food?
options: They are unable to find food on their own.
They must have a good memory for where things are located.
They never actually return to eat the food they hide.
They hide food only when they are not hungry.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文提到狼崽能把藏物转移到别处，并在数天后准确返回原地取回所藏之物；这一行为说明它们必须对位置有良好的记忆。

questions.question: In the last sentence, the word 'irrepressible' most nearly means
options: easily forgotten
rarely noticed
impossible to hold back
carefully planned
questions.explanation_zh: irrepressible 意为“无法抑制的、压不住的”。文中说梗犬、腊肠犬有 irrepressible compulsion to excavate（无法抑制的挖掘冲动），故最接近 impossible to hold back。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 18 的五个故事句式提升到 B2+：After I had had 写更早完成的事，I had left it 回溯东西原先的去处，As I was looking for 写寻找时被打断，In a few minutes ... returned 写短时间后的回转，gave it back to me 写归还。请用更抽象、更复杂的语境和更长的句子来仿写，保持过去完成时这一语法重点。

patterns.title: After I had had ...
patterns.source: After I had had lunch at a village pub, I looked for my bag.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 After I had had 说明“我已经做完某件事之后，又发生了后面的事”。
patterns.task_zh: 用 After I had had 写一件更早完成、且带有情绪或后果的事，然后描述随之而来的较抽象的行动或后果（如反思、寻找、道歉）。
patterns.sample: After I had had a long argument with my colleague about the budget, I anxiously looked for the report I had carelessly misplaced.
patterns.tip_zh: 第一个 had 是过去完成时助动词，第二个 had 表示 eat / experience；不要漏掉其中一个。

patterns.title: I had left it ...
patterns.source: I had left it on a chair beside the door.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 had left it 回头解释东西在更早的时候被放在哪里。
patterns.task_zh: 用 had left it 回头解释某个重要物品在更早的时候被你放在了哪里，并交代当时的背景或原因。
patterns.sample: I suddenly remembered that I had left it locked inside my desk drawer at the office on the evening before the holiday.
patterns.tip_zh: it 指代前一句已经提到的东西；后面常接 on / in / beside 等地点。

patterns.title: As I was looking for ...
patterns.source: As I was looking for it, the landlord came in.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式写“我正在找的时候，另一个动作发生了”，很有故事感。
patterns.task_zh: 用 As I was looking for 写你正在焦急寻找某个重要东西时，另一个出乎意料、可能带来压力的事件突然发生。
patterns.sample: As I was looking for the missing contract among the scattered files, my manager unexpectedly walked into the office and asked for an explanation.
patterns.tip_zh: As I was looking for 后面接要找的东西；逗号后写突然出现或发生的动作。

patterns.title: In a few minutes ... returned
patterns.source: In a few minutes he returned with my bag.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 In a few minutes 写“过了几分钟”，再用 returned 推动故事回来。
patterns.task_zh: 用 In a few minutes ... returned 写过了几分钟后，某人带着你以为弄丢的重要物品回来，并刻画当时的情绪转变。
patterns.sample: In a few minutes the security guard returned with the laptop I had abandoned in the conference room, looking faintly amused at my panic.
patterns.tip_zh: returned with 后面接带回来的东西；这能让故事从紧张转向安心。

patterns.title: gave it back to me
patterns.source: He gave it back to me.
patterns.focus_zh: gave it back to me 是很实用的“把东西还给我”。
patterns.task_zh: 用 gave it back to me 写在一番周折之后，某人找到了你贵重或要紧的东西并郑重地还给你。
patterns.sample: After patiently searching through the lost-property cupboard for nearly ten minutes, the receptionist finally found my passport and gave it back to me.
patterns.tip_zh: gave it back to me 可以接在 found / picked up / brought 等动作后面。
